sections.h2: What sets Rabun County apart for a house seller?
sections.html:
Rabun County is the most sparsely settled of the four counties in the Census Bureau's table, at 45.6 residents for each of its 370.13 land square miles. The tax commissioner's office sits in Clayton. The county counted 16,276 residents in 2010, 16,883 in 2020 and an estimated 17,764 in July 2025.

Age is the defining trait. People 65 and older are 31.5% of residents, children under 18 are 16.7%, and households average 2.24 people. Only 52.0% of those over 16 are in the labor force, though commutes are the shortest of the group at 23.1 minutes.

Money moves through the county differently too. Retail sales hit $448,203,000 in 2022, or $25,957 per resident, and hotels and restaurants sold $92,981,000. Medical and social service providers took in $69,267,000. Employers numbered 535 in 2023 with 5,271 jobs, up 5.3% in a year, and a payroll of $206,253,000.

sections.h2: What do Rabun County homes cost?
sections.html:
The middle value of a home that its owner occupies is $295,200, second to Pike among the four, and owners live in 77.1% of housing.

Median household income is $67,493. Mortgaged owners pay $1,481 a month, and owners with no loan pay $491. The county has 12,695 housing units but only 7,615 households, so many properties are not a household's main residence. If yours is one of them, it may not hold a homestead exemption, and the next owner's bill could differ from the one you pay now.

sections.h2: What do Rabun County's jobs and coverage figures say?
sections.html:
Two groups stand out. Residents under 5 are only 3.9% of the population, while 31.5% are 65 or older. Among people under 65, 19.0% have no health insurance, and labor force participation is 52.0%, with women at 47.2%.

Business ownership is common. The county has 2,100 businesses with no employees, against 535 with a payroll. Transportation and warehousing receipts were only $1,150,000 in 2022, far below its lodging and food sales. Computer ownership is 95.0% of households.

Density has barely moved: a 2010 density of 44.0 and a 2020 density of 45.6. A seller should price from nearby closed sales, not from county averages, because the spread between a village lot and mountain acreage can be wide.

The population is 92.5% White alone, with Hispanic or Latino residents at 9.8% and people born abroad at 6.6%. Another language is spoken at home by 8.7% of residents 5 and older. The county has 1,261 veterans.

Schooling is strong: 90.3% of adults 25 and over finished high school and 31.3% hold a bachelor's degree. Per person income is $43,928, and 11.7% of residents live in poverty. Broadband reaches 90.8% of households, the best coverage of the four. A 10.8% disability rate applies to residents under 65.

About 89.0% of residents kept the same address for a full year. For a seller, that points to a mostly settled community where a for-sale sign draws attention and word of mouth matters.

sections.h2: How do I reach Rabun County's tax offices?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner is at 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, Clayton, GA 30525, phone (706) 782-3613, with weekday counter hours that end at 4:30 pm, major holidays excluded.

  • Payments by mail: make checks payable to the Rabun County Tax Commissioner.
  • Payments online: cards cost 2.50% or a $1.25 minimum, and eChecks cost $1.50 each. A cart lets you pay several bills at once.
  • Assessors: values, returns, special programs and appeals.
  • Deeds: copies come from the deed room at the Rabun County Courthouse.

Bills are mailed to whoever owns the property. A lender with an escrow account will not get one, so send yours along.

sections.h2: When is Rabun County property tax due, and what happens late?
sections.html:
December 1 applies to real estate and business personal property. The county's property FAQ and the tax commissioner's site agree on that date.

Past that date, prime plus 3% accrues monthly, and 120 days later a 5% penalty joins it. A FIFA can be recorded once taxes have been unpaid more than 90 days, and the commissioner can levy on the property. The FAQ points out that the lien becomes a public record that credit bureaus may read.

The county accepts a United States Postal Service postmark, not a metered one. Mobile homes are billed in January, and the two county pages disagree on their due date, April 1 on one and May 1 on the other, so call (706) 782-3613 before paying one.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Rabun County value?
sections.html:
Get the written appeal to the assessors inside the 45-day window. The county's assessor FAQ says an appeal filed late is invalid.

It names three grounds: whether the property is taxable or exempt, whether it is valued in line with comparable property, and whether the dollar value is too high or too low. The assessors review it, and if nothing changes, the Board of Equalization hears the case. Rabun County Superior Court is the next level for either side.

The assessors remind owners that they follow the market and do not create it, using cost, market and income approaches. A recent sale price of a similar nearby house gives the strongest backing.

sections.h2: Which Rabun County assessment programs matter for land?
sections.html:
Land owners have more choices here than house owners. Each program below binds the property to its use under a 10-year covenant, and applications run January 2 through April 1.

  • Preferential agricultural: assessed at 30% of fair market value instead of 40%.
  • Conservation use: current use value replaces market value.
  • Environmentally sensitive: current use value for land kept natural and approved under state Department of Natural Resources rules.
  • Residential transitional: current use value where an area is moving away from residential use.

Standing timber is taxed once it is sold or harvested. Anyone selling land under a covenant should tell buyers, since the 10-year commitment affects what they can do with it.

sections.h2: How does Rabun County handle homestead and bill math?
sections.html:
Qualify by owning and living in the house as of January 1, then apply at the assessors. The tax commissioner's site says the form must arrive before April 1 for that year, while the assessor's page lists a different in-person window, so call (706) 782-3613 to confirm which one governs you.

Owners aged 62 can ask for an additional exemption. The bill itself is 40% of fair market value, minus exemptions, times the millage rate that the county commissioners and school board adopt. The county says the money pays for police, fire, schools, roads, bridges, water and parks.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Rabun County house with tax still owed?
sections.html:
Yes, with a payoff from the commissioner and the closing attorney handling it.

  1. Ask for the exact balance with interest and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. If the land is in a covenant program, share that with the buyer.
  4. List each payoff on the settlement statement.

When repairs or a long-empty house stall a standard listing, an as-is buyer lets you pick the closing day and pay off the tax from what you receive.

faqs.q: When do Rabun County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property, per the county FAQ and the tax commissioner's site.

faqs.q: Where is the Rabun County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: At 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, in Clayton. Call (706) 782-3613. Counter hours end at 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Rabun County?
faqs.a: A written appeal is due within 45 days of the notice. The assessor's FAQ treats later ones as invalid.

faqs.q: Can I pay Rabun County tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, online. The fee is 2.50% or $1.25 minimum for cards, and $1.50 for each eCheck.

faqs.q: Which Rabun County programs need a 10-year covenant?
faqs.a: Preferential agricultural, conservation use, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional assessments. Apply from January 2 to April 1.
